title: ADAS Level 2 does NOT mean self-driving
hook: Your 'Level 2 ADAS' car is not self-driving. Here's what it actually does in 30 seconds.
caption:
'Level 2 ADAS' is one of the most misunderstood lines in Indian car brochures 🛡️

Quick version:
• ADAS = Advanced Driver Assistance Systems
• Levels run from 0 to 5 (the SAE scale)
• Level 2 = the car can help with steering AND speed at the same time (for example, adaptive cruise control plus lane centring)
• BUT you are still the driver. Hands on the wheel, eyes on the road, always.

On Indian roads there's an extra catch. Features like lane keep assist depend on cameras reading lane markings. When markings are faded or missing, these features may not work reliably.

ADAS is a safety net, not a chauffeur.

Have you used ADAS on Indian highways? Tell me how it went 👇

Save this for the next time a salesperson says 'it drives itself'.
script:
SHOT 1 (0-2s): Face to camera in a parked car, hands clearly on the wheel. Text on screen: 'Level 2 ADAS ≠ self-driving'. VO: 'Your Level 2 ADAS car is NOT self-driving. Here's what it actually means.'

SHOT 2 (2-8s): Simple graphic of a ladder labelled 0 to 5. VO: 'ADAS levels go from 0 to 5. Zero means no automation, five means no driver needed at all.'

SHOT 3 (8-15s): Highlight Level 2 on the ladder, with icons for a steering wheel and a speedometer. VO: 'Level 2 means the car can help with steering and speed together. Think adaptive cruise control plus lane centring.'

SHOT 4 (15-21s): Back to you, tapping the wheel. Text: 'YOU are still the driver'. VO: 'But you are still fully responsible. Hands on the wheel, eyes on the road.'

SHOT 5 (21-27s): Your own footage of a road with faded lane markings, shot safely as a passenger or from a parked spot. VO: 'On Indian roads, faded lane markings can confuse the cameras, so features like lane keep assist may not work reliably.'

SHOT 6 (27-30s): Face to camera. Text: 'Safety net, not chauffeur'. VO: 'ADAS is a safety net, not a chauffeur. Follow for more car tech, explained simply.'
visual_brief: Shoot vertically (9:16) inside any car while it is parked; it doesn't need ADAS. Use simple self-made graphics in Canva or CapCut for the 0-5 ladder, in your brand colour. Shoot your own road footage only as a passenger or while parked. Never film while driving. Add bold captions on every shot, since most people watch muted.
